idea: Chinese supplier due diligence for European energy developers
buyer: European solar and battery project developers
pain: They procure from Chinese suppliers with no way to verify claims or compliance
channel: Father's network for access, industry contacts for demand
verdict: Real, current pain with compliance urgency; the buyer is adjacent rather than hers.

why.distribution: Developers are adjacent to her network; her father's side gives access to the subject, not the buyer.
why.demand: Forced labour and supply chain regulations make this close to mandatory for European developers.
why.fmf: Diligence framing plus China access; she is not a compliance or audit specialist.
why.revenue_structure: Repeat as procurement recurs, without contract.
why.defensibility: On-the-ground verification capability is genuinely hard to build.
why.leverage: Bespoke per supplier with local costs.
why.time_to_revenue: 3-6 months to build capability and first client.
why.tailwind: Supply chain compliance regulation is tightening in the EU with real penalties.
why.ceiling: £11k x 18 suppliers = £198k gross, less heavy local costs.

ceiling_arithmetic: £11k x 18 supplier reports = £198k gross, less ~35% local research and travel = £129k net. Delivery capacity and coordination bind hard. Realistic: 5-7 = £36-50k net.
carries: Regulatory compulsion rather than discretionary interest, plus access competitors lack.
kills: Heavy direct costs, coordination burden, and real reputational exposure if a report is wrong.
test: Ask two European developers how they currently verify Chinese suppliers.
test_pass: They admit they cannot and face audit pressure.
test_fail: They use a certification body already.
